This is one dissent recorded in a manifesto about sustaining human knowledge in the age of AI. Which fault line does it fall on?

Options:
- consent_or_payment: consent and payment mechanism: opt-in / levies / dues on existing text vs open training, pay at output, contracts for new work (Salib, Bratton, O'Reilly against the majority)
- model_in_loop: whether a model belongs in the checking loop or the room at all (Becker, Turkle)
- other: anything else

Text:

Tying payment or credentials to learning or grounding events undermines intrinsic motivation, cutting against per-event payment, and humans-know/machines-predict distinctions are too tidy.

It does not take a side in the consent-and-payment dispute over existing training text (opt-in or levies versus open training and paying at output), and it does not address whether a model belongs in the checking loop."}

parsed.why: The dissent argues that "tying payment or credentials to learning or grounding events undermines intrinsic motivation" and that "humans-know/machines-predict distinctions are too tidy." This is a motivational and epistemological objection to per-event rewards for learners. It does not take a side in the consent-and-payment dispute over existing training text (opt-in or levies versus open training and paying at output), and it does not address whether a model belongs in the checking loop.
